core_principles.text: Suspension push-ups require high motor control demands and the generation of muscle force to overcome the load and maintain stability.
Performing push-ups on unstable suspension straps increases the challenge of maintaining dynamic balance and stabilization while exposing the upper extremity to greater loads.
The 90-degree push-up test is a standard method for assessing upper body strength-endurance, requiring the lifter to lower until reaching a 90-degree angle.

specific_findings.text: In a study of 32 young men (17 suspension, 15 traditional), both groups improved physical performance after 10 weeks, but the suspension group showed a significantly greater improvement in the 90-degree push-up test (P < 0.05).

core_principles.text: Perform the traditional push-up on a stable surface with hands shoulder-width apart and fingers pointed forward.
Maintain a straight spine and keep the feet together during the movement.
Ensure the correct depth of 90 degrees of elbow flexion is acquired during each repetition.
For suspension push-ups, hang the slings at the shoulder opening with the hands positioned ten centimeters above the surface.

common_mistakes.text: Failing to acquire the correct depth of 90 degrees of elbow flexion.
Failing to maintain a straight spine during the movement.

specific_findings.text: In the suspension push-up protocol, the slings were hung at the shoulder opening while the participant's hands were positioned exactly ten centimeters above the surface.
The study protocol monitored body form and required repetitions to be repeated if the correct depth of 90 degrees was not acquired.

core_principles.text: Performing push-ups on an unstable suspension system forces the extremity musculature to play a greater role in joint stability and strains synergistic and stabilizing muscles.
Suspension push-ups can be utilized to increase the biceps brachii muscle's effectiveness in shoulder stabilization and motor control.

specific_findings.text: In a study of healthy young men, the suspension push-up group (n = 17) improved their 900 PU test score from 19.29 ± 10.14 to 31.47 ± 12.19, whereas the traditional push-up group (n = 15) improved from 19.40 ± 10.33 to 26.86 ± 12.60.

Suspension push-up training was significantly more effective in strength-endurance progress than traditional push-up training, showing a delta score of -12.18 ± 5.75 compared to -7.47 ± 6.12 (p = 0.033).

source: data\push-up\10-week suspension and traditional push-up training.pdf [part 7/12]

core_principles.text: When performing push-ups on an unstable surface, synergistic activation of both the shoulder muscles and the abdominal muscles is necessary to maintain a stable and proper body position.

specific_findings.text: In a study comparing suspension push-ups (n = 17) and traditional push-ups (n = 15) over 10 weeks, the suspension group reported significantly lower perceived exertion (CR-10 of 2.14 ± 2.46) than the traditional group (3.46 ± 1.94) by the 20th session.
Both suspension and traditional push-up training improve dynamic balance, but neither training modality shows superiority over the other.

source: data\push-up\10-week suspension and traditional push-up training.pdf [part 8/12]
